title: Security questionnaire surge-mode response & ops protocol for high-volume RFP windows
creator: Leah Kim
description: Background: Sales and Legal report repeated capacity spikes during enterprise procurement windows (multiple RFPs within 7 days). Current manual response process creates multi-week delays and inconsistent answers. Goal: design and pilot a 'surge-mode' ops protocol that combines an evidence-tiered answer model, temporary surge credits pricing, and a lightweight on-call SME rotation to deliver reliable SIG/CAIQ responses within target turnaround times while preserving legal and compliance controls. This ticket scopes the product + pricing experiment, authoring of the runbook, and integration with self-serve customer offers for credits.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence runbook published: Surge-mode triage matrix, stratified evidence bundles (Lite/Standard/Full), and legal guardrails
Pilot pricing experiment defined with A/B cohorts and telemetry segments (control: standard process, variant: surge credits + managed response)
Operational SLA targets agreed: T1 (high-priority) = 48 hours, T2 = 5 business days for Lite bundle responses
Automated intake form and priority scoring integrated into support workflow (PRD + intake form link)
Sales + Security + Legal signoff on limited self-attestation templates and tiered evidence packs
tasks: Draft PRD outlining surge-mode experiment, pricing triggers, and measurement plan
Work with Legal to produce pre-approved self-attestation templates for low-sensitivity questions
Design and document 3-tier evidence bundles (Lite / Standard / Full) and map to pricing credits
Implement intake form and priority-scoring rule in Zendesk/Support (integration spec in Confluence)
Pilot runbook rehearsals with 2 sales pods and security on-call rotation
Instrument dashboards for time-to-first-response, percent completed in SLA, revenue from surge credits

2025-02-25 Naomi Rivera (Security): Reviewed self-attestation templates. Feedback: require explicit contextual metadata and proof-of-control links for all 'yes' answers. Added checklist to Confluence page.

2025-02-27 Legal (J. Patel): Approved conditional use of pre-approved templates for 'Lite' evidence on non-controlled data. Legal requested limitation clause and audit-tail to be added to contracts. See PRD v0.3 in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_exAMPLE

2025-03-01 Engineering (SRE team): Scoped intake automation work. Proposed quick integration via webhook + GitHub issue template for security SME rotation. Proposed small service to track credit consumption. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/214

2025-03-03 Oscar Bennett: Roadmap update — planning pilot with two sales pods targeting three mid-market accounts each. Requesting approval for budgeted SME hours and pilot surge-credit SKU creation with Finance.
2025-03-03 Leah Kim: Noted risk — customers may view surge credits as gating access; propose UI language to frame as 'optional managed response service' and offer trial credit for initial RFPs.
decision_log: 2025-02-24: Decided to use a tiered evidence model instead of immediate full CAIQ completion for all requests — rationale: reduces average TAT and allows prioritization. Trade-off: may require follow-ups for high-sensitivity items.

2025-02-26: Pricing experiment will test two variants: (A) one-time surge credit purchase per RFP vs (B) prepaid monthly surge credits bundled with Dedicated reservations. Chosen to A/B test both concurrently with randomized assignment by region.
2025-02-28: Approved limited self-attestation use for Lite bundle under legal guardrails; full CAIQ still required for regulated customers. Chosen to accelerate low-risk deals.
2025-03-01: Implementation decision: automate intake + scoring, but keep final answer review manual by security SME for first 30 pilot responses.
risks: Over-automation could lead to inaccurate answers and compliance exposure — mitigated by manual review during pilot
Sales may over-commit SLA; requires strict intake scoring and guardrail enforcement
Pricing confusion between surge credits and existing evidence-credit products — requires clear sales collateral and SKU naming
metrics_and_kpis: Time-to-first-response (median) — target 24 hours for T1; 72 hours for T2
Percent responses meeting SLA — target >= 90% in pilot
Pilot conversion rate: percent of managed responses that convert to contract signature within 60 days
Revenue from surge credits and churn impact for customers using managed response
